Authors: Doug Doucette

Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Abstract: This paper argues that weather prediction and climate tipping are fundamentally different mathematical questions, even though they arise from the same physical system. The author uses a simplified three-variable climate model (Lorenz-84) to demonstrate this distinction. The core idea is that weather failure is defined relative to a specific forecast trajectory—how far an ensemble strays from that path. Climate failure, in contrast, is defined by a fixed, absolute threshold in a slowly changing variable, such as a long-term average temperature. Using these separate definitions, the paper shows that a model can exhibit chaotic, unpredictable weather (weather-thick) while simultaneously showing no sign of crossing a climate threshold (climate-thin). Authors: Doug Doucette

Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Abstract: This paper challenges the common assumption that a positive Lyapunov exponent—evidence of chaos—automatically signals operational failure. Instead, the author argues that chaos must be classified relative to four specific pieces of data: a projection that maps the full state onto relevant operational variables, a defined failure set, a range of possible initial states, and a finite time horizon. item.title: Ai-Dependent Judgment - How AI Reshapes the Formation and Transfer of Judgment
item.description:
Authors: Krishnan Vasudevan Anantha

Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: This paper examines how artificial intelligence changes the formation of judgment inside institutions even when formal decision authority resides with humans. It distinguishes between AI-supported, AI-influenced and AI-shaped judgment, and traces how AI can alter framing, evidence selection, interpretation and recommendation before a human review commences. The paper argues that conventional review structures may therefore preserve accountability in form without preserving substantive independent judgment, particularly as repeated use creates cumulative dependence, unauthorized or poorly observed AI use, and the propagation of framing, analytical and judgment errors across workflows. It proposes a framework for identifying where judgment is actually being formed, how machine influence accumulates, and when human review ceases to provide substantive independence.
